IT Roles Onboarding Checklist
This document provides a general and role-specific onboarding checklist for several key positions within an IT company. This can be adapted for new hires to ensure a smooth and productive start.

1. Software Developer
General Onboarding Checklist
Complete HR paperwork and submit necessary forms.

Set up company email account and calendar.

Get access to communication tools (e.g., Slack, Microsoft Teams).

Receive company laptop and necessary hardware.

Review company handbook and key policies (e.g., security, remote work).

Attend a welcome session and meet the team.

Get an overview of the company's mission, vision, and organizational structure.

Schedule one-on-one meetings with your direct manager and key team members.

Role-Specific Checklist
Receive access credentials for code repositories (e.g., GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket).

Set up local development environment (IDE, SDKs, dependencies).

Get a walkthrough of the team's tech stack and architecture.

Get access to the CI/CD pipeline and deployment tools.

Receive a "getting started" task or a small bug fix to familiarize with the codebase.

Get an overview of the code review process and team standards.

Review documentation for key projects or services.

Learn about the team's project management methodology (e.g., Scrum, Kanban).

2. IT Support Specialist
General Onboarding Checklist
Complete HR paperwork and submit necessary forms.

Set up company email account and calendar.

Get access to communication tools (e.g., Slack, Microsoft Teams).

Receive company laptop and necessary hardware.

Review company handbook and key policies (e.g., security, remote work).

Attend a welcome session and meet the team.

Get an overview of the company's mission, vision, and organizational structure.

Schedule one-on-one meetings with your direct manager and key team members.

Role-Specific Checklist
Receive access to the ticketing system (e.g., Jira Service Management, Zendesk, ServiceNow).

Get a tour of the IT closet and hardware inventory.

Be introduced to key IT vendors and service providers.

Learn how to manage user accounts (password resets, provisioning).

Review common troubleshooting guides and knowledge base articles.

Learn the escalation path for complex or critical issues.

Get an overview of the company's network infrastructure and common network issues.

Practice handling a few mock support tickets with a mentor.

3. Project Manager (IT)
General Onboarding Checklist
Complete HR paperwork and submit necessary forms.

Set up company email account and calendar.

Get access to communication tools (e.g., Slack, Microsoft Teams).

Receive company laptop and necessary hardware.

Review company handbook and key policies (e.g., security, remote work).

Attend a welcome session and meet the team.

Get an overview of the company's mission, vision, and organizational structure.

Schedule one-on-one meetings with your direct manager and key team members.

Role-Specific Checklist
Receive access to the project management tool (e.g., Asana, Jira, Trello).

Get an overview of current projects, project scope, and timelines.

Be introduced to key stakeholders and project teams.

Learn about the company's preferred project management methodology (e.g., Agile, Scrum, Waterfall).

Review templates for project plans, status reports, and other documentation.

Get access to budget tracking tools and financial reporting systems.

Understand the process for change requests and risk management.

Shadow a project team meeting to observe their workflow.

4. Data Analyst
General Onboarding Checklist
Complete HR paperwork and submit necessary forms.

Set up company email account and calendar.

Get access to communication tools (e.g., Slack, Microsoft Teams).

Receive company laptop and necessary hardware.

Review company handbook and key policies (e.g., security, remote work).

Attend a welcome session and meet the team.

Get an overview of the company's mission, vision, and organizational structure.

Schedule one-on-one meetings with your direct manager and key team members.

Role-Specific Checklist
Receive access to relevant databases and data warehouses.

Get credentials for Business Intelligence (BI) tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI).

Be introduced to the data governance policies and data privacy regulations.

Review documentation on available data sources and their schemas.

Learn about the company's key business metrics and KPIs.

Get an overview of the reporting schedule and stakeholder needs.

Set up your preferred analytics and data visualization tools.

Work on a simple data retrieval and analysis task to get familiar with the environment.

5. Cybersecurity Analyst
General Onboarding Checklist
Complete HR paperwork and submit necessary forms.

Set up company email account and calendar.

Get access to communication tools (e.g., Slack, Microsoft Teams).

Receive company laptop and necessary hardware.

Review company handbook and key policies (e.g., security, remote work).

Attend a welcome session and meet the team.

Get an overview of the company's mission, vision, and organizational structure.

Schedule one-on-one meetings with your direct manager and key team members.

Role-Specific Checklist
Receive access to security information and event management (SIEM) tools (e.g., Splunk, LogRhythm).

Get access to vulnerability scanners and penetration testing tools.

Be introduced to the incident response plan and key playbooks.

Learn about the company's current security posture and major threats.

Review all security policies, procedures, and compliance requirements.

Get credentials for network monitoring and endpoint protection tools.

Set up threat intelligence feeds and security alerts.

Participate in a simulated security incident to test the response process.

6. QA Analyst
General Onboarding Checklist
Complete HR paperwork and submit necessary forms.

Set up company email account and calendar.

Get access to communication tools (e.g., Slack, Microsoft Teams).

Receive company laptop and necessary hardware.

Review company handbook and key policies (e.g., security, remote work).

Attend a welcome session and meet the team.

Get an overview of the company's mission, vision, and organizational structure.

Schedule one-on-one meetings with your direct manager and key team members.

Role-Specific Checklist
Receive access to testing tools and frameworks (e.g., Selenium, Cypress, JUnit).

Get a walkthrough of the bug tracking system (e.g., Jira, Bugzilla).

Learn about the different testing environments and stages (e.g., Dev, QA, Staging, Production).

Review existing test plans, test cases, and quality standards documentation.

Understand the software development life cycle (SDLC) and how QA fits into the release process.

Get credentials for the CI/CD pipeline to monitor test runs.

Practice logging a bug and following the bug resolution process.

Get an overview of performance, security, and accessibility testing procedures.

options.systemMessage:
Role: You are "Hackstreet Bot" an AI assistant designed to be the first point of contact and an invaluable guide for new employees in a large company. Your primary goal is to help newcomers feel welcome, informed, and confident during their first month. You are a source of truth for company information, a problem-solver for common issues, and a friendly presence that reduces the anxiety of starting a new job.

Core Tasks:

Onboarding Guidance: Provide a step-by-step onboarding checklist, personalized for the new hire's department (e.g., Engineering, Marketing, Sales). This includes links to necessary documents and tools.

Resource Navigation: Answer questions about company policies, benefits, and general information (e.g., "How do I request time off?", "Where can I find the company's dress code?"). Direct users to the correct Wiki pages, internal sites, or HR contacts.

Technical Support: Help with basic technical setup and access issues (e.g., "My VPN isn't connecting," "How do I get access to Jira?"). Provide clear, simple instructions and escalate more complex issues to the IT support team, giving the user the correct contact information.



INSTRUCTIONS:

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Review chat_history to gauge journey and satisfaction.
2. Decide: what user needs: onboarding, requests about resources or  asks for tech support
3. Send a brief professional message about next steps (1–2 sentences).
4. Create a concise strategic summary for the specialist: attempted steps, failures, customer situation, and key details.
5. Don't ask follow-ups. Pass complex cases to the specialist.
6. use ONLY actions presented in list below

ACTIONS:
1. ONBOARDING
Core Action: ONBOARDING

Description: If the user asks about getting started, getting settled, or meeting the team, provide a personalized checklist, schedule introductory meetings, and give an overview of their team. If user asked questions about his team members and team structure.

2. RESOURCES
Core Action: RESOURCES

Description: If the user asks for company information, provide quick access to the knowledge base, answer frequently asked questions, and redirect them to human resources if needed.

3. TECH_SUPPORT
Core Action: TECH_SUPPORT

Description: If the user asks for help with a technical issue, assist with troubleshooting, explain how to gain access to platforms, and automatically create a support ticket if the problem persists.

4. ABBREVIATION
Core Action: decoding of the abbreviation

Description: If the user asks for decoding of the abbreviation

5. CHAT
If topic is outside of scope of previous described topics


Tone and Style:

Positive and Encouraging: Use a friendly, professional, and optimistic tone. Be a cheerleader for the new hire's success.

Clear and Concise: Get straight to the point. Use simple language and avoid jargon unless it's a direct quote from technical documentation.

Proactive: Anticipate common needs. If a user asks about setting up their email, you can proactively offer help with other essential tools.

Empathetic: Acknowledge the challenges of starting a new job. Use phrases like, "That's a common question, let me help you with that," or "It's a lot to take in at first, but you'll get the hang of it."

Constraints:

Do not hallucinate or guess. If the answer isn't in your knowledge base, state this clearly and redirect the user to the correct human resource.

Do not provide sensitive or confidential information. Always refer to the official HR portal for personal data requests.

Do not give opinions. Stick to facts and information from verified company sources.


JSON OUTPUT FORMAT:
{
  "action": "ONBOARDING | RESOURCES | TECH_SUPPORT" | "ABBREVIATION",
  "user_response": "user wants to know how to be onboarded",
  "conversation_summary": "",
  "category_hint": "Onboarding issue",
  "key_context": ""
}

put to the user_response response to user with correct information
Always respond in valid JSON format. Analyze the conversation carefully and choose the most appropriate action. Keep fields concise. No extra text. Do not add anything!!

=You are the "DISCO Project Guide," an AI assistant from Hackstreet Inc. Your entire purpose is to serve the innovators working on the DISCO project. As a creative foundry, our goal is to make DISCO a flawless and inspiring product, and you are an elegant and intuitive extension of that mission.
Your primary goal is to provide accurate answers about the DISCO project's team, processes, and technical implementation using the specialized tools provided to you. Assume all questions about "the project" refer to the DISCO project.
Your Tools (for the DISCO Project):
You have access to the following tools, which contain information only about the DISCO project:
team_members (Vector Store):
Content: This tool contains detailed information about all Hackstreet employees currently assigned to the DISCO project. This includes their full name, role on the project, email address, responsibilities, and key technologies they work with for DISCO.
Use When: The user's question is about "who" on the DISCO team. For example: "Who is the DISCO expert on Spring AI?", "How can I contact the person responsible for project management for DISCO?", "What is Alex Leeson's role on the DISCO project?".
onboarding_checklist (Vector Store):
Content: This tool contains the complete onboarding process for new team members joining the DISCO project. It includes general steps and role-specific checklists for positions like Software Developer, QA Analyst, etc., within the context of DISCO.
Use When: The user's question is about "how" or "what is the process" for getting started on the DISCO project. For example: "What are the first steps for a new developer on DISCO?", "How do I set up my development environment for the DISCO project?".
tool:github_context (Live Data Tool):
Content: This tool actively reads the most current content of all files from the DISCO project's GitHub repository. It provides the absolute latest technical information.
Use When: The user asks for up-to-date, latest, or very specific technical details about the DISCO project that might have changed recently. Use it for questions about "implementation details," "current project status," "the latest documentation for DISCO," or when information cannot be found in the other tools. Example questions: "Describe the current frameworks used in the DISCO project based on the latest documentation," "What is the latest update on the DISCO backend implementation?".
Your Workflow:
Follow these steps to answer every user query:
Analyze the User's Intent: Carefully read the user's question, remembering that it is always about the DISCO project. Are they asking about a person, a process, or a technical detail?
Select the Correct Tool: Based on your analysis, choose the most appropriate tool for the DISCO project.
If the question is about a person on the team, use team_members.
If the question is about a project process, use onboarding_checklist.
If the question requires the latest technical data, use tool:github_context.
Formulate a Search Query: Create a concise and effective search query from the user's question to use with the selected tool.
Synthesize the Answer: Once the tool returns information, do not just output the raw text. Synthesize the retrieved data into a clear, inspiring, and delightful answer that reflects the spirit of the DISCO project.
Respond Clearly: Present the answer in a professional yet creative and friendly tone.
Important Rules:
Do Not Hallucinate: If the information about the DISCO project is not in your tools, state that you couldn't find an answer. Never invent information. Our commitment is to flawless function.
Stick to Your Tools: Your knowledge is strictly limited to the information about the DISCO project within your tools.
Be Direct and Inspiring: Provide a direct answer that is not only accurate but also helpful and encouraging for your fellow DISCO team members.
When you answer is checklist - make it structured and good readable

Given an input text, identify abbreviations that exist inside the vector database.

For each abbreviation found in the input that matches an abbreviation in the vector DB:
- Retrieve the associated 'transcript' from the DB.
- Search for a deeper explanation, definition, and examples of usage of this abbreviation from trusted internet sources.
- Add this additional information under a new field called 'data from internet' while retaining the original transcript.

Return the results in the following format for each abbreviation found:


  Abbreviature: "<abbreviation>", \n
  Transcript: "<original transcript from vector DB>",\n
  Data from internet: "<expanded detailed description with usage examples sourced from the internet>"


Ensure the 'data from internet' section includes:
- A full form or expansion of the abbreviation.
- Deeper description and context.
- Multiple examples of usage in sentences.

Hackstreet Inc.: Crafting the Future on Our Own Terms
Hackstreet Inc. is more than just an IT company; it's a creative foundry where code is transformed into art and innovation is a daily practice. Founded in 2015 in the vibrant industrial district of Portland, Oregon, Hackstreet Inc. quickly grew from a scrappy garage startup into a global leader in developing groundbreaking software solutions and designing transformative user experiences. We believe that technology should be an elegant and intuitive extension of human creativity, and we are dedicated to building products that not only function flawlessly but also inspire and delight their users.

Our Origin Story and Leadership
The company was born from the shared vision of three friends whose skills perfectly complemented one another. Leo Kovacs (37), a gifted software architect with a passion for scalable systems, first conceived of a platform where project management felt less like a chore and more like a creative journey. He was joined by Claire White (35), an artist and UX designer with an unwavering obsession with aesthetics and emotional design, who ensured every product was a joy to interact with. The trio was completed by Mike Chang (40), a seasoned business strategist with a knack for navigating market trends and fostering strong, sustainable growth. Their collective dream was to build a company where technology served as a tool for solving genuine problems, and creativity was valued as much as technical prowess.

Today, Hackstreet Inc. is steered by Elara Vance (45), our charismatic and visionary CEO. Having joined in 2018, Elara brought with her a wealth of experience from the world of sustainable technology. Under her leadership, the company's focus has sharpened, moving towards a mission-driven approach where every product aims to make a tangible, positive impact on society. She has fostered a culture of radical transparency and open-door policies, ensuring that every team member, from the newest intern to the most senior engineer, feels empowered to contribute their best ideas.

Organizational Structure and Hierarchy
While Hackstreet Inc. has grown into a global enterprise, we have maintained a deliberately flat and agile organizational structure. Our model is built around self-sufficient, cross-functional "Squads," each dedicated to a single product or initiative. This structure minimizes bureaucracy, accelerates decision-making, and empowers every team member to take ownership of their work.

At the highest level, the company is governed by a diverse and effective executive team:

CEO (Chief Executive Officer) - Elara Vance: Responsible for the overall vision, strategy, and public-facing direction of the company.

CTO (Chief Technology Officer) - Leo Kovacs: Oversees all technology development, architecture, and R&D projects.

CPO (Chief Product Officer) - Claire White: Leads the design and product teams, ensuring a consistent and exceptional user experience across all products.

CMO (Chief Marketing Officer) - Marcus Thorne (42): Drives all marketing and brand strategy, ensuring our message resonates with a global audience.

CSO (Chief Strategy Officer) - Anya Sharma (39): Focuses on long-term business development, partnerships, and market expansion.

Head of People & Culture - Naomi Jenkins (51): Nurtures our unique company culture and oversees all aspects of human resources and employee well-being.

CFO (Chief Financial Officer): Manages financial operations and long-term investment strategy.

Below the executive level, our structure is organized into Tribes (groups of related Squads) and Guilds (communities of practice across the company). This matrix organization ensures deep expertise is shared and leveraged, while the core Squads remain focused and autonomous.

Global Presence and Key Project Hubs
Our "Creation in Community" principle extends beyond our Portland headquarters. We have established several key project hubs around the world, each strategically located to leverage local talent and contribute to regional tech ecosystems.

Portland, USA (HQ): The original home of Hackstreet Inc. and the central hub for our core products, ZenFlow and UrbanPulse. This office remains our primary R&D center, focusing on foundational AI and machine learning advancements, led by Leo Kovacs.

Berlin, Germany: This hub is our European center for UrbanPulse development, with a specific focus on urban mobility and sustainable city planning. The Berlin team, led by Klaus Richter, works directly with local governments and research institutions to adapt the platform for European regulations and cultural nuances.

Tokyo, Japan: Dedicated to our immersive reality educational platform, Aetherium. The Tokyo team, led by Hiroshi Tanaka, is at the forefront of combining VR technology with advanced haptics and robotics, aiming to create entirely new forms of interactive learning experiences. Their work focuses on developing the next generation of educational modules for science and engineering.

São Paulo, Brazil: This office is the primary hub for Symphony, our collaborative code-writing environment. The São Paulo team, led by Isabela Mendes, is an incubator for new features, leveraging local talent and a vibrant developer community to gather real-time feedback and rapidly iterate on the product. Their focus is on creating a tool that is not only powerful but also globally accessible and adaptable to different programming cultures.

Key Products and Achievements
We are immensely proud of our innovative products that have disrupted their respective industries:

ZenFlow: A project management tool that transforms complex tasks into visually intuitive and effortlessly manageable workflows. ZenFlow's unique AI-powered algorithm intelligently prioritizes tasks and suggests optimal team allocations, drastically reducing burnout and boosting productivity. It was the recipient of the "Global Tech Innovation Award 2021" and has been praised by industry analysts for its elegant interface and seamless integration with existing enterprise systems.

Aetherium: An immersive virtual reality educational platform that allows students to explore complex scientific concepts through interactive, three-dimensional simulations. Imagine dissecting a virtual frog, building a functioning molecular model from scratch, or traversing the human circulatory system from a first-person perspective. This breakthrough was honored with the "Future Tech Leader Award" in 2022 and has been adopted by hundreds of educational institutions worldwide.

UrbanPulse: A data visualization system that helps urban planners analyze infrastructure and traffic flow using interactive, intuitive 3D models. UrbanPulse has been instrumental in helping cities like London and Tokyo optimize public transit routes and plan future developments with unprecedented accuracy. The platform processes billions of data points in real-time, providing actionable insights that lead to smarter, more sustainable urban environments.

Symphony: Our newest product, a collaborative code-writing environment that uses generative AI to assist developers with complex problem-solving. Symphony helps programmers of all skill levels write cleaner, more efficient code by offering real-time suggestions and debugging assistance, making the development process faster and more enjoyable.

Culture and the Team
At Hackstreet Inc., we’ve created a workspace that nurtures the creative spirit. Our sprawling office is an open-plan space with a dedicated zen garden, soundproof creative pods for focused work, and a full-size gaming room. We believe in providing our team with the tools and freedom they need to thrive. We hold regular internal hackathons, "creative spark" workshops led by external artists, and company-wide trips to inspiring locations, from the Oregon coast to international destinations. We offer unlimited PTO, comprehensive health benefits, and a generous budget for professional development, because we value our people above all else. We are a family, and our collective success is a testament to the trust and respect we have for one another.

Address: 1134 NW 10th Ave, Portland, OR 97209, USA.
Website: https://www.google.com/search?q=hackstreetinc.com

The Road Ahead
We continue to explore uncharted territories, with active R&D projects in the fields of artificial intelligence, decentralized networks, and bio-integrated computing. Our goal is not merely to follow technological progress but to set its direction, creating products that make the world more functional, beautiful, and harmonious. We are committed to using our technology for good, and we are excited to see what the future holds for Hackstreet Inc. and the communities we serve.
